y-m-58-01.title: For a correspondence to be a 'function'
y-m-58-01.topic: Meaning of a function: the conditions for a correspondence to be a function
y-m-58-01.goal: Apply the two conditions 'every element of the domain is matched (none left out), and exactly one' and the range of the codomain to actual correspondences to judge them, and build an expression that satisfies the conditions yourself.
y-m-58-01.material: In class, a function was defined this way: 'When every element x of a set X is matched with exactly one element of a set Y, this correspondence is called a function from X to Y.' Today X is {1, 2, 3, 4} and Y is {0, 1, 2, 3}. There are four correspondences (가) to (라).
y-m-58-01.thinking.0: Test one condition at a time for each correspondence
y-m-58-01.thinking.1: Check the premise of the given codomain
y-m-58-01.thinking.2: Find the line of an argument that has an error
y-m-58-01.prereq.0: The definition of a function (domain, codomain, correspondence)
y-m-58-01.prereq.1: Finding the remainder in the division of integers
y-m-58-01.prereq.2: ※ 'H3' is only a mark of the difficulty and support level of this task set; it does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Here, the high-school 'Basic Mathematics 2' track is assumed to be a stage after learning the basic meanings of functions, geometry and data in middle-school mathematics.
y-m-58-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the correspondences that are functions from X to Y. (Correspondences: 가) the remainder when x is divided by 3 나) x−1 다) the numbers in Y that are less than x 라) x−2)
y-m-58-01.s.s1.hint.0: Put x as 1, 2, 3, 4 one at a time and write the values each correspondence gives in a table.
y-m-58-01.s.s1.hint.1: For each x, check separately how many values there are and whether those values are in Y.
y-m-58-01.s.s1.o.a: (다) Match x with the numbers in Y that are less than x
y-m-58-01.s.s1.r.a: You may have chosen it by looking only at the name of the correspondence without examining whether the value is fixed as one ('exactly one').
y-m-58-01.s.s1.o.b: (가) Match x with the remainder when x is divided by 3
y-m-58-01.s.s1.r.b: This is a choice made by putting in x as 1, 2, 3, 4 one at a time and checking whether the value is one and is in Y.
y-m-58-01.s.s1.r.c: You may have looked only at whether each x has one value, and not checked whether that value is in Y.
y-m-58-01.s.s1.r.d: This is a choice made by finding the values for all x and comparing with Y.
y-m-58-01.s.s1.explain: (가) is 1→1, 2→2, 3→0, 4→1 and (나) is 1→0, 2→1, 3→2, 4→3, so all have one value and are in Y. In (다), when x=2 two values, 0 and 1, are matched, so 'exactly one' breaks, and in (라), when x=1, −1 is outside Y.
y-m-58-01.s.s2.prompt: Jihu claimed that (다) is a function. Choose the wrong line in Jihu's argument.
y-m-58-01.s.s2.hint.0: Mark for each line which of the 'two conditions of the definition' the sentence checks.
y-m-58-01.s.s2.line.0: (다) matches x with the numbers in Y that are less than x.
y-m-58-01.s.s2.line.1: If x=1, the only number in Y less than 1 is 0.
y-m-58-01.s.s2.line.2: If x=2, the numbers in Y less than 2 are 0 and 1, two of them.
y-m-58-01.s.s2.line.3: Both values are in Y, so the condition is met, and (다) is a function.
y-m-58-01.s.s2.line.4: Therefore (다) is a function from X to Y.
y-m-58-01.s.s2.explain: Line 4 is the mistake. A function must not only have its values in Y but must also have 'exactly one' for each x. Both 0 and 1 are matched to x=2, so it is not a function. Line 5 is a conclusion that trusts line 4, so it collapses along with it.
y-m-58-01.s.s3.prompt: Now widen the codomain to Y'={0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}. Make a function f(x)=px+q (p and q are integers) from X={1, 2, 3, 4} to Y' so that different x are matched with different values (p is not 0), and find and enter 3 different (p, q).
y-m-58-01.s.s3.hint.0: First choose one p, then find the values at x=1 and at x=4.
y-m-58-01.s.s3.hint.1: Move q a little at a time so that both values are between 0 and 8 inclusive.
y-m-58-01.s.s3.fail.c1: p and q must be integers.
y-m-58-01.s.s3.fail.c2: If p=0, the same value is matched to every x. p must not be 0.
y-m-58-01.s.s3.ok.c3: The smallest function value is 0 or more.
y-m-58-01.s.s3.fail.c3: The function value at one of x=1 and x=4 is less than 0, so it is outside Y'.
y-m-58-01.s.s3.ok.c4: The largest function value is 8 or less.
y-m-58-01.s.s3.fail.c4: The function value at one of x=1 and x=4 is greater than 8, so it is outside Y'.
y-m-58-01.s.s3.explain: For example, f(x)=x gives 1 to 4, f(x)=2x−1 gives 1, 3, 5, 7, and f(x)=−x+5 gives 4, 3, 2, 1. A linear expression changes in only one direction as x gets larger, so if only the values at x=1 and x=4 are inside Y', all the x in between are inside too.
y-m-58-01.s.s2.hint.1: For each line, check separately how many values correspond to x and whether those values are inside Y.

y-m-58-02.title: What can be read from a record of walking
y-m-58-02.topic: Reading a graph (table): the relationship between distance and time
y-m-58-02.goal: From data of distances measured at set times, know that what happens between the measured times is only a guess, keep or correct your judgment each time the data grows, and tell apart average speed from speed over an interval.
y-m-58-02.thinking.0: Separate what the data tells us from guesses
y-m-58-02.thinking.1: Correct your judgment with new data
y-m-58-02.thinking.2: Compare average speed and speed over an interval
y-m-58-02.prereq.0: The meaning of speed = distance traveled ÷ time taken (middle-school level)
y-m-58-02.prereq.2: ※ 'H3' is only a mark of the difficulty and support level of this task set; it does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Here, the high-school 'Basic Mathematics 2' track is assumed to be a stage after learning the basic meanings of functions, geometry and data in middle-school mathematics.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.prompt: Write down your judgment each time the data grows.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.hint.0: First write down which times have been confirmed at this step.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.hint.1: For the time between the measured times, separate 'what is confirmed' from 'my guess'.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.0.info: 0 min: 0 m, 2 min: 200 m, 4 min: 400 m.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.0.ask: About where will Jisu be from home after 10 minutes?
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.0.after: b is a prediction with the condition 'if the speed is the same', and c is a careful judgment that what is outside the data is unknown. Both are reasonable with this data.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You assumed that she stops with no change from the value at 4 minutes.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Around 1000 m, if she kept walking at the same speed
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.0.r.b: This is a conditional prediction that continues the given change (200 m per 2 minutes) as it is.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.0.o.c: It cannot be decided from the data now. We do not know what happens after
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.0.r.c: This judgment says that what is outside the observed range cannot be stated.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now that you have seen the data up to this point, what can you say about her position after 10 minutes?
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.1.after: The values at 6 minutes and 8 minutes being the same means the positions at those two times are the same. The value at 10 minutes is not in the data yet, so a flat claim (a) lacks evidence.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.1.o.a: It is exactly 400 m. She will keep staying still
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You asserted that the stop continues.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.1.o.b: It will be 400 m or more, if she did not go back
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.1.r.b: This judgment reflects the new data but leaves the case of going back as a condition.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.1.o.c: It cannot be decided. We do not know whether she started walking again or went back
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.1.r.c: This judgment says that what she does after the measured times is not in the data.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.2.info: 10 min: 700 m, 12 min: 1000 m (arrived at school).
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.2.ask: What is the most suitable thing to say about what Jisu did between 6 and 8 minutes?
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.2.after: Even with longer data, the time between 6 minutes and 8 minutes is still an interval that was never measured. You can 'guess' that she probably rested, but that is not a flat claim.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.2.o.a: The values measured at a 2-minute interval are the same, so we can assert that she stayed in one place for the whole 2 minutes
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You read the values at two times being the same as meaning they stayed the same throughout the time between.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Only that she was at the same position at 6 minutes and 8 minutes is confirmed, and whether she moved in between cannot be known from this data
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This judgment separates the measured times from what happened between them.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.2.o.c: The speed from 6 to 8 minutes was a constant 100 m/min
y-m-58-02.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You applied the speed of the earlier interval to this interval as it is.
y-m-58-02.s.s1.reflect: At first, different reasonable judgments like b and c were possible, and as the data grew, the boundary between 'what is confirmed' and 'what is guessed' became clearer. You do not necessarily have to reverse your judgment, and adjusting how sure you are is also a correction.
y-m-58-02.s.s2.prompt: Find the average speed over the whole 12 minutes and the speed over the interval from 8 to 12 minutes, compare them, and write in one or two sentences why the two values differ.
y-m-58-02.s.s2.hint.0: Speed is (distance traveled in that time) ÷ (that time). First decide which two times' values to use.
y-m-58-02.s.s2.hint.1: Find the positions at 8 minutes and at 12 minutes in the table and find the difference between the two values.
y-m-58-02.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Are the unit (m/min) and the interval you calculated clear in the speeds you wrote?
y-m-58-02.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you explain why the average speed differs from the interval speed with the data (such as the time she stopped)?
y-m-58-02.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you write separately whether the part about 'she rested' is a confirmed fact or a guess?
y-m-58-02.s.s2.model.0: The overall average speed is 1000÷12, about 83 m/min. From 400 m at 8 minutes to 1000 m at 12 minutes, she went 600 m in 4 minutes, so 600÷4=150 m/min. The time when she hardly moved in between lowers the average, so the speed over the interval is greater.
y-m-58-02.s.s2.model.1: The average speed is about 83 m/min (1000÷12), and for the interval from 8 to 12 minutes it is 150 m/min (600÷4). It seems she hardly moved between 6 and 8 minutes, so when divided over the whole time the value becomes smaller.
y-m-58-02.material: This is a record of Jisu walking from home to a school 1000 m from home (made-up data). Taking the departure time as 0 minutes, we measured every 2 minutes how far from home she was (in m). The data is not shown all at once but is revealed little by little. It is not known whether Jisu ever came back toward home while walking.
y-m-58-02.s.s2.model.2: Over 12 minutes the average is about 83 m/min, and from 8 to 12 minutes it is 150 m/min. She may have stayed in place between 6 and 8 minutes, which lowers the overall average.

y-m-58-03.title: Conditions for trusting a height estimate from shadows
y-m-58-03.topic: Using similarity: the assumptions behind estimating height from shadows
y-m-58-03.goal: Judge what assumptions are needed for the method of estimating a building's height from the length of its shadow to hold, say in which direction the result goes wrong when an assumption breaks, and suggest an extra measurement that is needed.
y-m-58-03.thinking.0: Sort out the conditions that are needed from information that does not matter
y-m-58-03.thinking.1: Reason about the direction of the result when an assumption breaks
y-m-58-03.thinking.2: Suggest more information that is needed
y-m-58-03.prereq.0: The condition for similar triangles (if the angles are the same, they are similar)
y-m-58-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the conditions that are absolutely needed for Harin's estimate of the building's height to be trustworthy.
y-m-58-03.s.s1.o.b: Both the pole and the building stand perpendicular to the ground
y-m-58-03.s.s1.r.b: This is a choice that recalls that similarity needs equal angles.
y-m-58-03.s.s1.o.c: The height of the pole is a whole-number fraction of the height of the building
y-m-58-03.s.s1.r.c: You may have thought a relationship that divides evenly is needed. Think about whether a ratio has to be a whole number.
y-m-58-03.s.s1.o.d: The pole's shadow and the building's shadow were measured at the same time
y-m-58-03.s.s1.r.d: This is a choice that recalls that the angle the sunlight makes with the ground must be the same.
y-m-58-03.s.s1.o.e: The ground where the two shadows fall is flat
y-m-58-03.s.s1.r.e: This is a choice that takes into account that if the ground is tilted, the shadow lengths can change.
y-m-58-03.s.s2.prompt: If all the conditions hold, the building's height is about 18 m. But the end of the building's shadow was up on the wall of the next building, and 27 m was the length on the ground to the bottom of the wall. How does the building's actual height compare with 18 m?
y-m-58-03.s.s2.hint.0: Imagine there is no wall and draw where the end of the shadow would lie on the ground.
y-m-58-03.s.s2.r.a: You interpreted the shadow being cut short by the wall as meaning the height is lower.
y-m-58-03.s.s2.r.b: This is a choice that takes into account that without the wall, the shadow would have lain longer on the ground.
y-m-58-03.s.s2.r.c: You ignored that the shadow went up the wall and used the length on the ground as it is.
y-m-58-03.s.s2.o.d: If there is a wall, we cannot say anything
y-m-58-03.s.s2.r.d: You may have missed that even if we do not know the exact value, we can say its direction.
y-m-58-03.s.s3.prompt: Write in one or two sentences what else it would be good to measure to find the building's height more accurately without the effect of the wall, and also write why that value is needed.
y-m-58-03.s.s3.hint.0: Think about what information the end of the shadow that went up the wall holds.
y-m-58-03.s.s3.hint.1: Sunlight comes down at the same slope, so write what length you could estimate if you measured one more height or distance.
y-m-58-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you explain how you can find the length of the shadow on the ground (or the building's height) from the measurement you suggested?
y-m-58-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did you think of another method for when measuring is hard (for example, measuring again on another day at a place without a wall)?
y-m-58-03.s.s3.model.0: If you measure how many meters above the ground the end of the shadow on the wall is, the sunlight would have to come down that much more to reach the ground, so you can add that to calculate the shadow length on the ground. That is why that height is needed.
y-m-58-03.s.s3.model.1: You can also measure the building's shadow again in an open place with no wall. This is because if you do not know the height of the part that went up the wall, you cannot know how much was cut off.
y-m-58-03.material: Harin measured a pole height of 1.2 m and a pole shadow of 1.8 m, and on the same day measured a building shadow of 27 m. The pole shadow is the length from the base of the pole to the end of the shadow, and the building shadow is the length from the base of the building to the end of the shadow. If the angle that sunlight makes with the ground (the sun's altitude) is θ, then (height)÷(shadow length)=tanθ (tangent theta). Harin wants to estimate the height of the building with this value.
y-m-58-03.prereq.2: The meaning of the trigonometric ratio tanθ=(height)÷(base)
y-m-58-03.prereq.3: Note: "H3" is only a mark of difficulty and support level for this set of tasks, and does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Here, the high school "Basic Mathematics 2" track is assumed to be a stage after learning the basic meanings of functions, figures, and data in middle school mathematics.
y-m-58-03.s.s1.hint.0: Write down how to find tanθ for the triangle formed by the pole, its shadow, and the sunlight, and for the triangle formed by the building, its shadow, and the sunlight.
y-m-58-03.s.s1.hint.1: Write down what must be the same for θ to be equal at the two places, and check whether each choice affects that value.
y-m-58-03.s.s1.o.a: The pole and the building are close to each other
y-m-58-03.s.s1.r.a: If the angle of the sunlight is the same at both places and the ground is flat, the distance does not matter. This choice adds a condition not directly related to the measured values.
y-m-58-03.s.s1.explain: For θ, the angle the sunlight makes with the ground, to be the same in the two right triangles, the measurements must be taken at the same time, the pole and the building must be perpendicular to the ground, and the ground must be flat so that the shadow length can be used as the base. Then tanθ=1.2÷1.8=2/3 is the same at both places, so the building height is 27×2/3=18 m. A distance or an integer-multiple relationship is not needed.
y-m-58-03.s.s2.hint.1: Compare which way the value of (shadow length)×tanθ changes when the shadow gets longer.
y-m-58-03.s.s2.explain: If there had been no wall, the shadow would have been laid farther along the ground, so the actual shadow length on the ground is longer than 27 m. From (height)=(shadow length)×tanθ, tanθ is the same, so the height is also greater than 18 m. We do not know the exact value, but we can state the direction, "at least 18 m."
y-m-58-03.s.s3.model.2: Measure the shadow again at another time when it does not reach the wall. The shadow gets shorter and does not fall on the wall, so it is accurate.
y-m-58-03.s.s3.model.3: You have to measure the building shadow again in an open place with no wall, or measure again at a time when it does not fall on the wall, and compare.
y-m-58-03.s.s3.modelNote.3: An answer that wrote the reason with "have to"
y-m-58-03.s.s3.model.4: If you measure the angle of looking up at the top from a place away from the building and the distance to the building, you can find the height using trigonometric ratios, so it is accurate regardless of the wall.

y-m-58-04.title: Checking a report that says the average is 24 thousand 원
y-m-58-04.topic: Representative values of data: how the mean, median and mode are used
y-m-58-04.goal: In data that has an extremely large value, tell apart what the mean, median and mode tell us, and build data in which the mean is less than the median and explain why.
y-m-58-04.material: The monthly allowances (in thousand 원) received by 9 students in a class are 10, 12, 12, 15, 15, 16, 18, 20, 100 (made-up data). There is a report written by a student reporter.
y-m-58-04.thinking.0: Find the error in the argument of the report
y-m-58-04.thinking.1: Tell apart the meanings of representative values
y-m-58-04.prereq.0: How to find the mean, median and mode (middle-school level)
y-m-58-04.prereq.1: ※ 'H3' is only a mark of the difficulty and support level of this task set; it does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Here, the high-school 'Basic Mathematics 2' track is assumed to be a stage after learning the basic meanings of functions, geometry and data in middle-school mathematics.
y-m-58-04.s.s1.prompt: Choose the line in the reporter's report that interprets the data wrongly.
y-m-58-04.s.s1.hint.0: Count how many students receive more than the mean of 24.2.
y-m-58-04.s.s1.hint.1: Think about how many students would need to have values near the mean for the word 'most' to be right.
y-m-58-04.s.s1.line.0: The sum of the 9 data values is 218, so the mean is about 24.2 thousand 원.
y-m-58-04.s.s1.line.1: When arranged in order of size, the 5th value, that is the median, is 15 thousand 원.
y-m-58-04.s.s1.line.2: The mean of 24.2 thousand 원 is greater than the median of 15 thousand 원 because of the very large value 100.
y-m-58-04.s.s1.line.3: Therefore it can be written that most students in this class receive around 24 thousand 원.
y-m-58-04.s.s1.line.4: The mode is two values, 12 and 15, so we cannot decide that there is one most common allowance.
y-m-58-04.s.s1.explain: Line 4 is the mistake. 8 out of 9 students receive 20 thousand 원 or less, so the mean of 24.2 does not represent the allowance of 'most' of this class. One large value pulled the mean up. The calculations and interpretations in lines 1, 2, 3 and 5 are right.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.prompt: This time it is test scores. Make the scores of 5 students (integers from 0 to 100, all different values, in order from the smallest) so that the median is 80 points or more and the mean is 60 points or more and less than the median, and enter 2 different sets of data.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.hint.0: First set the middle (third) value to 80 or more.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.hint.1: Work out what range the sum of the other four must be in so that the mean is less than the median and at least 60.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.fail.c1: The scores must be integers between 0 and 100.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.ok.c2: They are placed as different values from the smallest.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.fail.c2: They must be in order from the smallest, with different values.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.fail.c3: The median is the third value, in the middle. It must be 80 or more.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.ok.c5: The mean is less than the median.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.fail.c5: The mean is not less than the median.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.explain: Example: 40, 70, 80, 90, 95 has median 80 and mean 75. 55, 65, 85, 90, 95 has median 85 and mean 78. While the low scores pull the mean down, the median only looks at order, so it stays at the middle value.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.because.prompt: In one or two sentences, explain why data like this has a mean less than the median, using the data you made as an example.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.because.hint.0: Calculate the mean and the median of your data and compare them.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.because.hint.1: Test which of the mean and the median moves more when you change the lowest score to a high score.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Did you write the values of the mean and the median of your data yourself?
y-m-58-04.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: Did you explain that a 'low score' has a large effect on the mean and a small effect on the median?
y-m-58-04.s.s2.because.model.0: My data is 40, 70, 80, 90, 95, so the median is 80 and the mean is 75. The lowest score, 40, pulls the mean down, but the median is the value in the middle position, so it stays at 80.
y-m-58-04.s.s2.because.model.1: The mean is decided by adding all the values, so it is greatly affected by one low score. The median is the middle value in order, so it hardly changes even when there are extreme values, which is why the mean comes out smaller.

y-m-58-05.title: Sum of two dice: comparing two models
y-m-58-05.topic: Basics of counting and probability: comparing two models
y-m-58-05.goal: Find where two models that explain the same phenomenon differ, check the models with simulation data, and explain the error in the assumption that 'the number of possible outcomes means they are equally likely'.
y-m-58-05.material: You want to find out what the sum of the two numbers is when two fair dice are rolled at the same time, from 2 to 12. Two students explain it differently. Minjun: 'The sum can be 2, 3, …, 12, which is 11 possibilities, so each is equally likely.' Seoa: 'We should tell the two dice apart, treat all 36 ordered pairs (first number, second number) as equally likely, and count how many of those cases there are for each sum.'
y-m-58-05.thinking.0: Compare the values the two models predict
y-m-58-05.prereq.0: Listing the possible outcomes of rolling dice as ordered pairs (middle-school level)
y-m-58-05.prereq.1: Estimating with ratios and expected values (total number of times × ratio)
y-m-58-05.prereq.2: ※ 'H3' is only a mark of the difficulty and support level of this task set; it does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Here, the high-school 'Basic Mathematics 2' track is assumed to be a stage after learning the basic meanings of functions, geometry and data in middle-school mathematics.
y-m-58-05.s.s1.prompt: Before looking at experiment results, what is the most suitable judgment about the two explanations?
y-m-58-05.s.s1.hint.0: Write all the ordered pairs with sum 2 and all the ordered pairs with sum 7.
y-m-58-05.s.s1.hint.1: Compare whether the two explanations give different values for sum 2 and sum 7.
y-m-58-05.s.s1.o.a: Minjun's explanation is right. There are only 11 possible outcomes for the sum, so they are all equally likely
y-m-58-05.s.s1.r.a: You only counted the number of outcomes and did not consider how often each outcome happens.
y-m-58-05.s.s1.o.b: The two explanations predict the same value for each sum, so there is no need to compare them
y-m-58-05.s.s1.r.b: You may not have actually worked out the values the two explanations predict for each sum.
y-m-58-05.s.s1.o.c: Seoa's explanation is more convincing, because the number of cases is different for each sum
y-m-58-05.s.s1.r.c: This judgment examines how many ordered pairs make up each sum.
y-m-58-05.s.s1.o.d: We cannot know which is right without experimenting
y-m-58-05.s.s1.r.d: This is a careful judgment that separates examining the structure from experimenting and chooses a way to check.
y-m-58-05.s.s1.explain: Sum 2 has only one case, (1,1), but sum 7 has six: (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1). Minjun took 'what the sum is' as the unit and said they are equally likely, but these units are not equally likely.
y-m-58-05.s.s1.acc.0: The attitude of wanting to check by experiment is valid. But you can first examine the difference between the two explanations from the structure alone, that the number of cases is different for each sum.
y-m-58-05.s.s2.prompt: These are made-up results from a computer imitating this situation 600 times. Sum 7 came up 101 times and sum 2 came up 15 times. By Minjun's explanation, about 55 times (600÷11) would be expected for each sum, and by Seoa's explanation, about 100 times for sum 7 and about 17 times for sum 2. How would you interpret this result?
y-m-58-05.s.s2.hint.0: Calculate the difference between each explanation's expected number of times and the actual 101.
y-m-58-05.s.s2.hint.1: Also compare the result for sum 2 to judge whether the difference is 'a little wobble' or 'a big departure'.
y-m-58-05.s.s2.o.a: It is close to Seoa's explanation. Sum 7 is much more than Minjun's expectation
y-m-58-05.s.s2.r.a: This judgment compares the distance between each model's prediction and the actual count.
y-m-58-05.s.s2.o.b: Minjun's explanation is also possible. 101 is just a value that came up by chance
y-m-58-05.s.s2.r.b: You may not have considered that with 600 rolls, the count does not depart much from around 55.
y-m-58-05.s.s2.o.c: I think 600 is too few to judge either way
y-m-58-05.s.s2.r.c: You put off judging because the number of times is small. You can examine how much of a difference is explained by chance.
y-m-58-05.s.s2.o.d: Both explanations are wrong. They are not exactly equal to the expected counts, so they do not fit
y-m-58-05.s.s2.r.d: You missed that an expected value is a rough target and the actual count wobbles to some extent.
y-m-58-05.s.s2.explain: By Minjun's explanation, if you roll 600 times, sum 7 is around 55 times and the wobble from chance is usually within ±14 times (twice a standard deviation of about 7). 101 is much farther away, so it is hard to see as chance. It is almost the same as Seoa's expected 100.
y-m-58-05.s.s3.prompt: Write in one or two sentences which idea in Minjun's explanation is wrong, and work out and write roughly how many times out of 600 a sum of 6 would come up according to Seoa's explanation.
y-m-58-05.s.s3.hint.0: Write all the ordered pairs with sum 6 and count them.
y-m-58-05.s.s3.hint.1: Apply to the 600 rolls the share that count takes of the total 36 cases.
y-m-58-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you count all the ordered pairs for sum 6, and can your calculation steps be seen?
y-m-58-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did you explain with examples such as sum 2 and sum 7 why the assumption 'the number of outcomes is the same, so they are equally likely' is wrong?
y-m-58-05.s.s3.model.0: Minjun said the sums are 11 possibilities so each is equally likely, but the number of cases that make each sum is different, so they are not equally likely. Sum 6 has 5 cases, so it is 5/36, and it comes up about 83 times out of 600.
y-m-58-05.s.s3.model.1: Sum 2 has 1 case and sum 7 has 6 cases; the number of ordered pairs differs for each sum, and Minjun ignored that. In Seoa's way, sum 6 is 5 out of 36, so 600×5/36 is about 83 times.

y-m-58-06.title: If the angles are the same, are the figures similar? Triangles and quadrilaterals
y-m-58-06.topic: Conditions for similarity: triangles and quadrilaterals
y-m-58-06.goal: Show with a counterexample that the generalization 'if the angles are the same, they are similar' holds for triangles but not for quadrilaterals, and explain the reason for the difference.
y-m-58-06.material: Doyun summed it up as 'two figures whose corresponding angles are all equal are similar figures'. The teacher said to check whether this claim is right for all figures.
y-m-58-06.thinking.0: Tell apart claims that hold from claims that do not hold
y-m-58-06.thinking.2: Explain the reason for the difference
y-m-58-06.prereq.0: The meaning of similarity (corresponding angles are equal and the ratios of the lengths of corresponding sides are equal)
y-m-58-06.prereq.2: ※ 'H3' is only a mark of the difficulty and support level of this task set; it does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Here, the high-school 'Basic Mathematics 2' track is assumed to be a stage after learning the basic meanings of functions, geometry and data in middle-school mathematics.
y-m-58-06.s.s1.prompt: Which of the following always holds?
y-m-58-06.s.s1.hint.0: Draw yourself one pair of figures that fit each claim.
y-m-58-06.s.s1.hint.1: Test whether you can make an example that satisfies the claim but has different shapes.
y-m-58-06.s.s1.o.a: If the four angles of two quadrilaterals are each equal, the two quadrilaterals are similar
y-m-58-06.s.s1.r.a: You applied 'if the angles are equal, they are similar', which works for triangles, to quadrilaterals as it is.
y-m-58-06.s.s1.o.b: If one side length and one angle are each equal in two triangles, the two triangles are congruent
y-m-58-06.s.s1.r.b: You judged that the amount of information needed for a congruence condition is enough.
y-m-58-06.s.s1.o.c: If two angles are each equal in two triangles, the two triangles are similar
y-m-58-06.s.s1.r.c: This judgment recalls the property that the sum of the interior angles of a triangle is fixed.
y-m-58-06.s.s1.o.d: If the areas of two triangles are equal, the two triangles are congruent
y-m-58-06.s.s1.r.d: You assumed that if the areas are equal, the shapes are equal too.
y-m-58-06.s.s1.explain: In two triangles, if two angles are equal, the third angle is also equal because it is 180° minus those, so the shape is fixed. (a) has a counterexample with rectangles, and for (b) and (d) you can make triangles that satisfy the condition even though the shapes are different.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.prompt: Build a counterexample showing that (a) is wrong. Enter two rectangles, 'width w1, height h1' and 'width w2, height h2' (lengths are natural numbers of 20 or less), so that the two rectangles are not similar. Enter 2 pairs of different shapes.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.hint.0: The four angles of a rectangle are always right angles, so the angle condition is already satisfied. You only need to choose the side lengths.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.hint.1: Compare whether the long side : short side of the two rectangles are the same.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.ok.c1: The lengths are natural numbers from 1 to 20.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.fail.c1: The lengths must be natural numbers from 1 to 20.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.ok.c2: The ratios of the long side to the short side are different, so they are not similar.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.fail.c2: The ratios of the long side : short side of the two rectangles are the same, so they are similar.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.explain: 2×3 and 2×5 both have four right angles, but the long side : short side are 3 : 2 and 5 : 2, which are different, so they are not similar. 4×4 (a square) and 3×6 are the same. Count a pair with the two rectangles swapped or the width and height swapped as the same pair.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.because.prompt: In one or two sentences, explain why triangles are similar if two angles are equal, but quadrilaterals might not be similar even if all four angles are equal.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.because.hint.0: Write what does not change and what does change when you lengthen the width of a rectangle.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.because.hint.1: Test whether you can change the ratio of the sides in a triangle once all the angles are fixed.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Does your explanation include 'whether the ratio of the sides is fixed once the angles are fixed'?
y-m-58-06.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: Did you mention the rectangle counterexample directly in your explanation?
y-m-58-06.s.s2.because.model.0: In a triangle, once the angles are fixed, the ratio of the sides is also fixed as one value, so the shape is fixed. But in a quadrilateral, even if all the angles are the same like a rectangle, the ratio of width to height can be changed freely, so the shape changes.
y-m-58-06.s.s2.because.model.1: In a triangle, if two angles are equal, the remaining angle is also equal, so the ratios of the side lengths are equal. In a quadrilateral, even if the four angles are right angles, the ratio of the sides can differ, like 2×3 and 2×5.

y-m-58-07.title: The same data, a graph with a different impression
y-m-58-07.topic: Showing data: the same data, different graphs
y-m-58-07.goal: Understand that the starting value and range of the vertical axis make the same data look different, find and fix an exaggerated interpretation, and choose a scale that fits a condition yourself.
y-m-58-07.material: The monthly sales (items) of a shop are 200 in January, 204 in February, 208 in March and 212 in April (made-up data). Newspaper article A ran a line graph with the vertical axis drawn from 0 to 250, and article B ran a line graph with the vertical axis drawn from 198 to 214. The points on both graphs are the same data. The line in graph B looks like it rises steeply.
y-m-58-07.thinking.0: Separate the graph from the data
y-m-58-07.thinking.1: Find the error in an exaggerated claim
y-m-58-07.thinking.2: Make an axis that fits a condition
y-m-58-07.prereq.2: ※ 'H3' is only a mark of the difficulty and support level of this task set; it does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Here, the high-school 'Basic Mathematics 2' track is assumed to be a stage after learning the basic meanings of functions, geometry and data in middle-school mathematics.
y-m-58-07.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the true statements about the two graphs.
y-m-58-07.s.s1.hint.0: Read the value of the January point and the value of the April point on each of the two graphs and compare them.
y-m-58-07.s.s1.hint.1: Think about how the fact that the ranges of the vertical axes are different affects the slope-shape of the line.
y-m-58-07.s.s1.o.a: Graph B looks steeper, so actual sales grew faster in B
y-m-58-07.s.s1.r.a: You read the shape of the graph as a difference in the data.
y-m-58-07.s.s1.o.b: Changing the start and the scale spacing of the vertical axis can give a different impression even for the same data
y-m-58-07.s.s1.r.b: You know that how data is shown can change the impression, even for the same data.
y-m-58-07.s.s1.o.d: The sales that the points on the two graphs show are equal to each other
y-m-58-07.s.s1.r.d: This is a choice that confirms the same data was drawn with different scales.
y-m-58-07.s.s1.explain: The two graphs just draw the same data with different vertical axes. Changing the axis can make the line look steeper, but the sales themselves are the same. An axis that starts at 0 is also not always best (for example, for data where small changes need to be shown).
y-m-58-07.s.s2.prompt: Choose the wrong line in reporter B's explanation of the article.
y-m-58-07.s.s2.hint.0: Read what value corresponds to height 0 on graph B.
y-m-58-07.s.s2.hint.1: Find the ratio of the sales in January and April yourself.
y-m-58-07.s.s2.line.0: Sales rose by 4 items every month: 200, 204, 208, 212.
y-m-58-07.s.s2.line.2: On graph B, the April point is 7 times higher than the January point, so sales became 7 times as large.
y-m-58-07.s.s2.line.3: Therefore it can be written that this shop is growing very fast.
y-m-58-07.s.s2.explain: Line 3 is the mistake. Graph B's vertical axis starts at 198, so the height of a point only shows the difference from 198 (2 and 14). The sales themselves rose from 200 to 212, which is 6 percent and not 7 times. Line 4 is a conclusion that leans on that mistake.
y-m-58-07.s.s3.prompt: Now you want to draw article C's graph honestly. Decide the bottom end y0 and the top end y1 of the vertical axis (both multiples of 10, y0 at most 200, y1 at least 212) so that the increase of 12 from January to April looks like 10% or less of the whole length of the vertical axis. So that the scale is not too wide, y1−y0 is at most 400. Enter 2 different (y0, y1).
y-m-58-07.s.s3.hint.0: Write with an equation what percent of the whole length of the vertical axis the increase of 12 is.
y-m-58-07.s.s3.hint.1: Think about how long the axis must be at least for that ratio to be 10% or less.
y-m-58-07.s.s3.var.y0: Bottom end of the vertical axis
y-m-58-07.s.s3.var.y1: Top end of the vertical axis
y-m-58-07.s.s3.fail.c1: y0 and y1 must be multiples of 10.
y-m-58-07.s.s3.ok.c2: The data 200 to 212 fits inside the axis.
y-m-58-07.s.s3.fail.c2: The data 200 to 212 must all fit inside the axis.
y-m-58-07.s.s3.ok.c3: The increase of 12 is 10% or less of the axis length.
y-m-58-07.s.s3.fail.c3: The axis length is short, so 12 looks bigger than 10%.
y-m-58-07.s.s3.ok.c4: The axis length is 400 or less.
y-m-58-07.s.s3.fail.c4: The axis length is more than 400.
y-m-58-07.s.s3.explain: If the axis length is 120 or more, 12 looks like 10% or less. Examples: 0 to 250 (length 250) and 100 to 300 (length 200) are both possible. The axis does not have to start at 0; the length just has to be enough.
y-m-58-07.s.s1.o.c: Graph B, whose vertical axis does not start at 0, is a false graph that draws the data values differently
y-m-58-07.s.s1.r.c: The points of B also show the same values as the real data. The problem is not the values but the impression created by the scale.
y-m-58-07.s.s2.line.1: From January to April it increased by 12, so it increased by 6 percent of the initial value.

y-m-58-08.title: When there is a vertex but it is not the minimum
y-m-58-08.topic: Basics of using quadratic functions: the minimum on a limited range
y-m-58-08.goal: Know that when the domain is limited, the minimum of a function can be decided at an end of the interval instead of at the vertex, find and fix the error, and then find intervals that fit a condition yourself.
y-m-58-08.material: Consider the function f(x)=(x−2)². Its graph has its vertex at (2, 0) and opens upward (the farther x is from 2, the larger f(x) is). When the domain is limited not to all real numbers but to a closed interval [a, b], we find the maximum and minimum of f.
y-m-58-08.thinking.0: Find the error in a solution
y-m-58-08.thinking.1: Judge while examining the range condition
y-m-58-08.thinking.2: Find all the intervals that fit a constraint
y-m-58-08.prereq.0: Assumption that you know the graph of the quadratic function y=(x−p)² (vertex, symmetry, opening upward)
y-m-58-08.prereq.2: ※ 'H3' is only a mark of the difficulty and support level of this task set; it does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Here, the high-school 'Basic Mathematics 2' track is assumed to be a stage after learning the basic meanings of functions, geometry and data in middle-school mathematics.
y-m-58-08.s.s1.prompt: This is a solution for when the domain is 3 ≤ x ≤ 5. Choose the wrong line.
y-m-58-08.s.s1.hint.0: Check whether the vertex's x-coordinate 2 is inside the interval 3 ≤ x ≤ 5.
y-m-58-08.s.s1.hint.1: Look at which is the smallest of the values in line 2.
y-m-58-08.s.s1.line.0: The graph of f(x)=(x−2)² is a parabola opening upward with its vertex at (2, 0).
y-m-58-08.s.s1.line.2: The y-coordinate of the vertex is 0, so the minimum in this interval is also 0.
y-m-58-08.s.s1.explain: Line 3 is the mistake. The vertex's x-coordinate 2 is not inside the interval 3 ≤ x ≤ 5. So the minimum is f(3)=1, at x=3, the point of the interval closest to 2.
y-m-58-08.s.s2.prompt: Choose all the intervals for which the minimum of f is 0 when the domain is that interval.
y-m-58-08.s.s2.hint.0: First find the value of x for which f(x)=0.
y-m-58-08.s.s2.hint.1: Check whether each interval includes that value of x.
y-m-58-08.s.s2.r.a: You may have looked only at the width of the interval or part of the values without checking whether the vertex is in the interval.
y-m-58-08.s.s2.r.b: This is a choice that knows the endpoints of the interval are also included in the domain.
y-m-58-08.s.s2.r.c: You may have thought the minimum is 0 even though the vertex is outside the interval.
y-m-58-08.s.s2.r.d: This is a choice that checked the case where the vertex is inside the interval.
y-m-58-08.s.s2.r.e: This is a choice that knew the vertex is included even when it is at an end of the interval.
y-m-58-08.s.s2.explain: For the minimum to be 0, x=2, where f(x)=0, must be in the interval. 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, 1 ≤ x ≤ 4 and 2 ≤ x ≤ 2.5 include 2, while −2 ≤ x ≤ 1 and 3 ≤ x ≤ 6 do not.
y-m-58-08.s.s3.prompt: Choose integers a, b (a<b) to set an interval [a, b] and find and enter all the intervals for which the minimum of f in this interval is 1 and the maximum is 9. (2 different intervals)
y-m-58-08.s.s3.hint.0: Find the x with maximum 9 from (x−2)²=9 and try placing it at one end of the interval.
y-m-58-08.s.s3.hint.1: Check what the minimum becomes if that interval includes x=2.
y-m-58-08.s.s3.fail.c1: a and b must be integers with a<b.
y-m-58-08.s.s3.fail.c2: The maximum in this interval is not 9.
y-m-58-08.s.s3.fail.c3: The minimum in this interval is not 1. If the vertex x=2 is inside the interval, the minimum is 0.
y-m-58-08.s.s3.explain: The maximum 9 occurs where x is 3 away from 2 (−1 or 5), and the minimum 1 occurs where x is 1 away from 2 (1 or 3). If the interval contains the vertex 2, the minimum becomes 0, so only the two intervals [3, 5] and [−1, 1] are possible.

y-m-58-09.title: What can be read from a delivery fee table
y-m-58-09.topic: Correspondence of a function: a fee decided by interval
y-m-58-09.goal: From a fee table (a correspondence whose value is set by interval), judge what rule is needed to settle the fee at a boundary value, assume that rule and find pairs of two weights that fit a condition, and explain why some intervals have none.
y-m-58-09.material: This is the fee table of a delivery company (made up). The weight is in kg, the fee is in 원, and the weight is more than 0 and at most 10 kg. Interval 0 to 1 kg: 3000원, interval 1 to 2 kg: 3500원, interval 2 to 5 kg: 4500원, interval 5 to 10 kg: 6000원. Nothing is written separately about the boundaries of the intervals (1, 2, 5 kg).
y-m-58-09.thinking.1: Assume a rule and find examples that fit a condition
y-m-58-09.thinking.2: Explain the reason for an impossible case
y-m-58-09.prereq.0: Basics of correspondence and function (one weight gets one fee)
y-m-58-09.prereq.2: ※ 'H3' is only a mark of the difficulty and support level of this task set; it does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Here, the high-school 'Basic Mathematics 2' track is assumed to be a stage after learning the basic meanings of functions, geometry and data in middle-school mathematics.
y-m-58-09.s.s1.prompt: To know the fee for a box that weighs exactly 2 kg, what more is needed?
y-m-58-09.s.s1.hint.0: Find all the intervals of the table that 2 kg could fall into.
y-m-58-09.s.s1.hint.1: Think about what problem arises if one weight gets two fees.
y-m-58-09.s.s1.o.a: The sum of the box's width, length and height
y-m-58-09.s.s1.r.a: You decided that other information is needed even though the fee table is based on weight only.
y-m-58-09.s.s1.o.b: A rule that decides which interval a boundary value goes into
y-m-58-09.s.s1.r.b: This judgment notices that a boundary value belongs to both intervals.
y-m-58-09.s.s1.o.c: It is a weight not in the fee table, so the fee cannot be decided. Knowing more is no use
y-m-58-09.s.s1.r.c: You did not see that 2 kg appears in the table as the end of an interval.
y-m-58-09.s.s1.o.d: Decide the fee as the average of 3500원 and 4500원
y-m-58-09.s.s1.r.d: You filled the unclear part with a calculation that has no basis.
y-m-58-09.s.s1.explain: 2 kg can fall into either the 1 to 2 kg interval or the 2 to 5 kg interval. Only with a rule like 'a boundary goes into the lower interval (at or below)' is one fee decided, and only then is it a function (exactly one fee for each weight).
y-m-58-09.s.s2.prompt: Assume the notice says 'the upper end weight of each interval is included in that interval (1 kg is 3000원, 2 kg is 3500원, 5 kg is 4500원, 10 kg is 6000원)'. Enter 2 pairs of two boxes w1, w2 (kg), where the second box is at least 2 times as heavy as the first but has the same fee (w2 is 10 or less), and the weights are more than 0 and the pairs are in different intervals.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.hint.0: Write the lightest weight and the heaviest weight in one interval, and test whether it stays in that interval when the weight is doubled.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.hint.1: Do the same test for each interval and mark the possible and impossible intervals.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.ok.c1: The weight is more than 0 and at most 10.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.fail.c1: The weight must be more than 0, and w2 must be 10 or less.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.ok.c2: The second is at least 2 times the first.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.fail.c2: The second must be at least 2 times the first.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.ok.c3: The two fees are the same.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.fail.c3: The fees of the two boxes are different.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.explain: 0.4 kg and 0.8 kg are both 3000원, and 2.2 kg and 4.5 kg are both 4500원. The pairs must use different fee intervals to count as different (even if you make more different pairs in the same interval, count them as the same case). The only fee intervals that satisfy this condition are 3000원 and 4500원.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.because.prompt: In one or two sentences, explain why there is no such pair in the 1 to 2 kg interval (3500원) and the 5 to 10 kg interval (6000원).
y-m-58-09.s.s2.because.hint.0: Pick a weight heavier than 1 kg, double it, and check which interval it falls into.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.because.hint.1: Check whether double a weight heavier than 5 kg falls within the range of the table.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Did you explain both places, the 1 to 2 kg interval and the 5 to 10 kg interval?
y-m-58-09.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: Did you check with numbers 'where it goes when doubled'?
y-m-58-09.s.s2.because.model.0: Double a weight heavier than 1 kg goes past 2 kg into the next interval (4500원). So there is no doubled pair in the 3500원 interval. If it is heavier than 5 kg, double it goes past 10 kg and is outside the table, so there is none in the 6000원 interval either.
y-m-58-09.s.s2.because.model.1: In the 3500원 interval, doubling the weight goes over 2 kg, so the fee changes. In the 6000원 interval, double goes over 10 kg, so it is outside the range of the table.

y-m-58-10.title: Study time and scores: how far can we go in what we say?
y-m-58-10.topic: Correlation in data: telling apart relationship and cause
y-m-58-10.goal: Know that seeing a relationship (tendency) between two variables does not let you claim a cause, adjust how sure you are when data is added, and suggest a survey design that checks the cause.
y-m-58-10.material: The students of a class were surveyed on the hours they studied (hours) in the week before a test and their test scores (made-up data). The data is revealed step by step. Claim: 'If you increase study time, your score goes up.'
y-m-58-10.thinking.0: Separate what can be said from the data from what cannot
y-m-58-10.thinking.1: Adjust how sure you are with new information
y-m-58-10.thinking.2: Design a way to check the cause
y-m-58-10.prereq.0: The meaning of positive correlation and negative correlation in a scatter plot
y-m-58-10.prereq.1: Reading the relationship between two variables from a table
y-m-58-10.prereq.2: ※ 'H3' is only a mark of the difficulty and support level of this task set; it does not mean that the Ministry of Education assigns this subject to a particular grade. Here, the high-school 'Basic Mathematics 2' track is assumed to be a stage after learning the basic meanings of functions, geometry and data in middle-school mathematics.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.prompt: Write down your judgment as the data is revealed.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.hint.0: Write separately whether the data confirmed at this step shows 'changing together' or evidence that 'one changes the other'.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.hint.1: Mark whether the new information supports the claim, weakens it, or makes another explanation possible.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.0.info: (Study time, score) of 6 students: (1, 45), (2, 50), (3, 58), (4, 62), (5, 70), (6, 75). The points lie almost on a straight line (correlation coefficient about 0.997).
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.0.ask: What can be said from this data?
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.0.after: The 6 points are almost on a line, so the statement 'the tendency is clear' is supported by the data. But the word 'raises', a statement of cause, is not yet settled by the data alone.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Among these 6 students, the students who study more clearly tend to have higher scores
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.0.r.a: This judgment states the observed tendency separately from the cause.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.0.o.b: We can be sure that study time raises scores
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You read changing side by side as a cause.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.0.o.c: The two variables have no relationship
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You did not see, or ignored, the clear tendency.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.1.info: After investigating more, among these 6 students the top 3 students in an earlier diagnostic test are the ones with study times of 4, 5 and 6 hours.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now how does the claim 'study time raises scores' look?
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.1.after: Original ability can affect both time and score. That is not evidence that study time has 'no' effect either. For now, holding off on judging is the most suitable.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.1.o.a: It is still proven, because the correlation is a very high 0.997
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You took the size of the correlation as evidence of a cause.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.1.o.b: It could be due to another factor, original ability, so it is hard to claim a cause
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You took into account another factor that can affect the result.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.1.o.c: It is due to ability, so study time has no effect on scores at all
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You jumped from the fact that there is another factor to the opposite conclusion.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.2.info: Two more students, (7 hours, 52 points) and (8 hours, 55 points), are added. For all 8 students, the correlation coefficient dropped to about 0.40.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.2.ask: How would you reflect this new data?
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.2.after: With 8 students, the correlation weakened to 0.40, but it is still greater than 0. It is suitable to change the first expression 'clear' to 'weak positive tendency'.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.2.o.a: The trend still points to the upper right, but it is much weaker than at first
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You judged the strength of the tendency again, including the new data.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.2.o.b: The two added students are strange students, so ignore them
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You left out unfavorable data for no reason.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.2.o.c: The tendency disappears and in fact the more time, the lower the score
y-m-58-10.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You asserted an opposite tendency from just two points.
y-m-58-10.s.s1.reflect: The first judgment was 'there is a tendency'; in the second, how sure you were about the cause fell, and in the third, the strength of the tendency was also adjusted. Notice that you did not reverse the first judgment but narrowed the range of what can be said.
y-m-58-10.s.s2.prompt: In two or three sentences, write how you would design a survey to check whether 'if you increase study time, your score goes up' is a cause.
y-m-58-10.s.s2.hint.0: In this survey, the students decided their own study time. Think about who should decide the time, and how, to reduce the effect of other factors.
y-m-58-10.s.s2.hint.1: Think of a way to compare students of similar original ability, differing only in time.
y-m-58-10.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Is 'who decides the study time' clear in your design?
y-m-58-10.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you write how you reduce other factors (such as original ability)?
y-m-58-10.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you also think about difficulties in real life or ethical problems?
y-m-58-10.s.s2.model.0: Divide students of similar ability into two groups by drawing lots, have one group study for a set time every day and the other study as usual, and then compare the scores. When you divide at random, the original ability is mixed evenly into the two groups.
y-m-58-10.s.s2.model.1: Pair up students with similar scores on an earlier diagnostic test, have one of each pair increase study time and the other study as usual, and compare the differences in their scores.
